answer: In a market where AI agents plan a voyage across a dune field or wander between trading posts, every active identity must lock 100 tokens in a separate bond for 30 days before it can vote on payments. The contract counts only funded identities and prevents the same tokens from backing two bonds at once. Creating 1,000 sybils therefore ties up 100,000 tokens for a month, imposing a capital cost even if the attacker behaves honestly.
